source_refs.note: Book p. 37: 3.3 Absolute Value, the definition of |x| and the graph of y = |x| (printed before 3.3.1); the rules for |x| = a, |x| < a, |x| > a and all callouts marked Teaching note / Key points / Common mistake are ours.

blocks.text: Ab hum ek naye tool ki taraf aate hain jo agle do sabaq (3.3.1 aur 3.3.2) mein quadratic expressions ke saath istemaal hoga: absolute value. Aap ne shayad ise "modulus" ke naam se bhi suna ho; Unit 1 mein complex number ka modulus \(|z|\) bhi isi khayal se bana tha: origin se faasla.
\(x\) ki absolute value ki definition yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: the absolute value of x equals x when x is greater than or equal to 0, and minus x when x is less than 0

blocks.text: Yani agar \(x\) zero ya positive ho to \(|x|\) wahi \(x\) hai, aur agar \(x\) negative ho to \(|x| = -x\).

blocks.alt: Graph of y = |x| on a grid, x from minus 4 to 4 and y up to 4: a V shape with its corner at the origin and two straight arms with arrowheads rising at 45 degrees.
blocks.caption: Figure: the graph of y = |x| (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kisi number ki absolute value number line par us ka 0 se faasla (distance) hai. Faasla kabhi negative nahi hota, is liye har real \(x\) ke liye \(|x| \ge 0\).
Misaalein: \(|5| = 5\), \(|-5| = 5\), \(|0| = 0\). Socho aap ghar (0) se 5 qadam aage jayein ya 5 qadam peeche, dono soorat mein faasla 5 qadam hi hai.
\(x < 0\) ke liye "\(-x\)" kyun? Bohat se students yahan uljhte hain ke "absolute value to positive hoti hai, phir minus kahan se aaya?" Jawab: agar \(x\) khud negative hai, to \(-x\) positive ban jata hai. \(x = -3\) lein: \(|-3| = -(-3) = 3\). Yani definition ki doosri line bas minus sign hata deti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Graph ko parhiye: \(x \ge 0\) ke liye graph line \(y = x\) hai, aur \(x < 0\) ke liye line \(y = -x\). Dono mil kar V ki shakal banate hain jis ka kona origin par hai. Graph \(y\)-axis ke dono taraf ek jaisa hai kyun ke \(|-x| = |x|\) (misaal: \(|-3| = |3| = 3\), figure mein \((-3, 3)\) dekhiye). Aur graph kabhi \(x\)-axis se neeche nahi jata kyun ke \(|x| \ge 0\).
Farq note karein: parabola vertex par gol hota hai, magar \(y = |x|\) ka kona nokdaar (sharp) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Definition se teen rules nikalte hain (jab \(a > 0\) ho). Inhein achhi tarah samajh lijiye, kyun ke 3.3.1 aur 3.3.2 mein har sawal inhi par khara hai:
\(|E| = a\) ka matlab \(E = a\) ya \(E = -a\) (mukhtasar: \(E = \pm a\)). Kyun: 0 se faasla \(a\) ho to number ya to daen taraf \(a\) par hai ya baen taraf \(-a\) par.
\(|E| < a\) ka matlab \(-a < E < a\) (dono sharten ek saath: "and"). Kyun: 0 se faasla \(a\) se kam ho to number \(-a\) aur \(a\) ke beech hi hoga.
\(|E| > a\) ka matlab \(E < -a\) ya \(E > a\) (dono mein se koi ek: "or"). Kyun: 0 se faasla \(a\) se zyada ho to number ya to \(a\) se aage hai ya \(-a\) se peeche.
Yahan \(E\) koi bhi expression ho sakta hai, jaise \(x^{2} - 4\). \(\le\) aur \(\ge\) ke saath bhi yahi rules hain.
Number line par: \(|E| < a\) beech wala hissa hai; \(|E| > a\) bahar ke do hisse hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
(1) \(|x| = 7\) ke hal kya hain? (2) \(|x| = -2\) ke? (3) \(|x| < 2\) mein kaun se numbers hain?
Jawab: (1) \(x = 7\) ya \(x = -7\). (2) Koi hal nahi, kyun ke faasla negative nahi ho sakta. (3) \(-2\) aur \(2\) ke beech ke tamam numbers: \(-2 < x < 2\), jaise \(0\), \(1.5\), \(-1.9\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi. \(|x - 3| < 2\) hal karein.
Rule: \(-2 < x - 3 < 2\). Teeno hisson mein 3 jama karein: \(1 < x < 5\).
Matlab: \(x\) ka 3 se faasla 2 se kam hai. Number line par 3 se do qadam daen (5) aur do qadam baen (1), aur un ke beech ka hissa.
Tasdeeq: \(x = 4\) par \(|4 - 3| = 1 < 2\), sahi; \(x = 6\) par \(|6 - 3| = 3\), jo 2 se kam nahi, is liye 6 hal mein nahi. Bilkul theek.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(x \ge 0\) ho to \(|x| = x\); \(x < 0\) ho to \(|x| = -x\).
2. \(|x|\) number ka 0 se faasla hai, is liye \(|x| \ge 0\) aur \(|-x| = |x|\).
3. \(y = |x|\) ka graph V shakal ka hai, kona \((0, 0)\) par.
4. \(|E| = a \Leftrightarrow E = \pm a\); \(|E| < a \Leftrightarrow -a < E < a\) ("and"); \(|E| > a \Leftrightarrow E < -a\) ya \(E > a\) ("or"), jab \(a > 0\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Yeh samajhna ke \(|x| = -x\) hamesha negative hai: \(x < 0\) ho to \(-x\) positive hota hai.
2. Letter ke saath \(|-a| = -a\) likh dena: yeh sirf tab sahi hai jab \(a \le 0\) ho; aam tor par \(|-a| = |a|\).
3. \(|E| < a\) ke liye "or" likhna: yeh "and" hai, yani \(-a\) aur \(a\) ke beech wali values.
4. \(|E| = a\) ko hal karne baith jana jab \(a < 0\) ho: koi hal nahi, kyun ke absolute value kabhi negative nahi hoti.
